Constitution of 1776 Art. 3: 'shall consist of seven Representatives to be chosen for each county annually'. Delaware had three counties (Art. 4 fixes the 9-member Council at three per county); 7x3=21 is derived from the per-county rule — the constitution states no total.
Constitution of 1776 Art. 4: upper house named 'The Council'; 'consist of nine members; three to be chosen for each county'. Recorded under chamber=senate for comparability.

Constitution of 1792 Art. II Sec. 2: 'There shall be seven representatives chosen in each county; until a greater number of representatives shall by the general assembly be judged necessary'. 7x3=21 derived from the per-county rule.

Constitution of 1792 Art. II Sec. 3 (Thorpe vol. 1): 'There shall be three senators chosen in each county.' Three counties; 3x3=9 derived. Same section lets the general assembly increase the number (senate never greater than one-half nor less than one-third of the house).

Amendments to the Constitution of 1790 ratified December 17; 1808: 'The senate shall be composed of one member from each election district ... except the district formed by the parishes of Saint Philip and Saint Michael; to which shall be allowed two senators'. 44 election districts plus one extra for Charleston = 45; derived from the district list in Art. I Sec. 3. MID-DECADE CHANGE: the old senators' seats were vacated the day before the second Monday of October 1810; so 37 applied earlier in 1810 and 45 from the October 1810 election.
